overview: Chile is a long, narrow country on the western side of South America, between the Andes and the Pacific Ocean. Its capital and largest city is Santiago. Chile won independence from Spain in 1818. It is one of the world's biggest producers of copper, and it also owns Easter Island, far out in the Pacific, which is famous for its giant stone statues.

geography.text: Chile is more than 4,000 kilometres long but on average less than 200 kilometres wide. In the north is the Atacama Desert, one of the driest places on Earth. The centre has a mild climate and most of the people, while the south breaks up into forests, fjords, glaciers and islands all the way to Cape Horn. The Andes run along the whole eastern border.

history.text: The Mapuche people resisted Spanish conquest in southern Chile for centuries. Chile won independence in 1818 and expanded north after defeating Peru and Bolivia in the War of the Pacific. In 1973 a military coup overthrew President Salvador Allende, and General Augusto Pinochet ruled until democracy returned in 1990.

events.title: War of the Pacific
events.text: Chile defeats Peru and Bolivia and gains their nitrate-rich coast.

events.title: Valdivia earthquake
events.text: The strongest earthquake ever recorded strikes southern Chile.

events.title: Democracy returns
events.text: Pinochet hands over to an elected president.

government.text: Chile is a presidential republic. The President is elected every four years and cannot serve two terms in a row. Congress has a Chamber of Deputies and a Senate. Chileans voted on two proposed new constitutions in 2022 and 2023 and rejected both.

economy.text: Chile is the world's largest producer of copper, which makes up a large share of its exports. It is also a major producer of lithium, wine, salmon, grapes and cherries. It has long been one of the most stable and prosperous economies in Latin America.

culture.text: Chile has two winners of the Nobel Prize in Literature, the poets Gabriela Mistral and Pablo Neruda. Easter Island, or Rapa Nui, with its giant moai statues, belongs to Chile. The country stretches about 4,300 km from north to south but averages only about 175 km wide.

items.title: Moai
items.text: Nearly 1,000 giant stone statues on Rapa Nui.

items.title: Atacama Desert
items.text: One of the driest places on Earth, home to major telescopes.

items.title: Pablo Neruda
items.text: The poet won the Nobel Prize in 1971.

sport.text: Football is the most popular sport. Chile won the Copa América in 2015 and 2016, both times beating Argentina in the final on penalties. Tennis and skiing are popular, and Chile hosted the 1962 World Cup.

items.text: Chile hosted the men's World Cup.

items.title: Nicolás Massú
items.text: Won two Olympic tennis golds in 2004.
